_note: Which kinds of place may stand next to which. The per-area `gates` tables say what an area opens onto; this says what the world will tolerate having built there, which is a different question — a coven can reach a town in one gate without either table ever naming the other, because a third area put them side by side. Both layers apply: `gates` weights the roll, this re-weights it against what is already on the ground.
_radiusNote: Slack, in lattice slots, for counting two cubes as neighbours. The gap between cubes is 1, so 2 means 'touching, or one cube's breathing room apart'. This reads cubes, which is allocation. Distance between rooms is still hop count and always will be.

depthGate._note: Gates from the Hub, not tiers. An archetype outside its band is never rolled there at all, which is how a coven stays a thing you find rather than a thing you trip over.

affinity._note: affinity[candidate][neighbour] multiplies the candidate's gate weight for every already-placed neighbour of that kind. 1 is neutral and is the default for any pair not named here, so only real opinions need writing down. 0 forbids outright. The lookup tries the reverse pair too, so each opinion is written once.
